newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian farm lobby calls for trade push in Rio.
newsitem.headline: Australian farm lobby calls for trade push in Rio.

text.p: Australia's National Farmers' Federation (NFF) strongly supported pressure from the Cairns Group of agricultural free traders to seek meaningful liberalisation in the forthcoming multilateral trade round, NFF president Donald McGauchie said on Wednesday.
McGauchie was speaking ahead of the Australia-led Cairns Group's annual ministerial meeting on June 5 and 6 in Rio de Janeiro.
The 15-member Cairns Group will thrash out a strategy aimed at broadening, deepening and accelerating outcomes of the Uruguay Round of the GATT, he said in a statement.
The multilateral trade round is scheduled to start before the end of 1999.
Full implementation of Uruguay Round commitments for free world agricultural trade was estimated to be worth about A$1 billion a year in additional Australian exports by 2000, McGauchie said.
Among issues which remained to be addressed were high tariffs, non-tariff barriers and export subsidies, he said.
"We must continue to work hard to eliminate these impediments to our farm exports and Australia is looking particularly hard at the EU for substantial reductions in agricultural subsidies," he said.

McGauchie said he would welcome intensification of the campaign for further liberalisation of agriculture at the Rio de Janeiro meetings by its chairman, Australia's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade Tim Fischer.
